name: Numbat-multiome ATAC-bin
tagline: Published haplotype-aware joint inference; local comparison requires prerequisites.

steps.title: Prepare inputs
steps.text: Count fragments in genomic bins, obtain SNP-level allele counts and phase, and construct a defensible normalized reference profile.

steps.title: Define hidden states
steps.text: The published expanded-state hidden Markov model (HMM) represents candidate dosage and haplotype-fraction states along the chromosome.

steps.title: Score bin depth
steps.text: A Poisson-lognormal emission models each bin count: a Poisson sampling distribution has a variable lognormal rate, allowing baseline coverage, library size and dosage to influence expected counts and variability.

steps.title: Score phased alleles
steps.text: A beta-binomial emission models phased haplotype counts conditional on total allele observations. It allows more variability than a fixed-fraction binomial; sparse allele counts give weak evidence.

steps.title: Combine across neighbors
steps.text: The HMM combines emission scores with transitions that favor state persistence while allowing changes. Inference sums probability over possible neighboring state paths to estimate state uncertainty; this is model-based integration, not independent confirmation of depth by alleles.

steps.title: Interpret relative to reference
steps.text: Compare inferred events and uncertainty with the reference and independent validation; audit the exact implementation treatment of gaps and missing observations.

example.title: Depth and alleles together
example.setup: Illustrative bins have relative depths 1.0, 1.1, 0.5, 0.5; covered SNPs in the last region favor one phased haplotype.
steps: Compare emissions for a persistent baseline with a change after bin 2.
Combine Poisson-lognormal depth and beta-binomial allele emission scores with transitions across neighboring bins; sum over possible state paths when calculating state probabilities.
Report a candidate boundary and uncertainty relative to the reference.
example.interpretation: These numbers illustrate reasoning, not a Numbat fit or proof of an absolute deletion.

needed: Defensible reference and exact count provenance
adaptation.first_experiment: Audit barcode joins, phase and reference eligibility before any comparator run.
adaptation.success: A reproducible prerequisite report and, if feasible, comparison against independent truth.

cautions: MCF10-A is a development dataset; its identity does not establish normal or diploid truth.
AT is summed SNP-site depth and may count one molecule at multiple sites; do not assume it is independent of bin depth.
Missing allele observations are not balanced observations; exact implementation behavior needs audit.
Depth and allele signals can share fragments, so their agreement is not automatically independent confirmation; audit the published model assumptions for this assay.

name: Masked count changepoint with conditional alleles
tagline: Proposed depth-first segmentation, with alleles only when the joint measurement is justified.

steps.title: Keep the genomic grid
steps.text: Retain coordinates, observed zero counts, callable spans, exposure and explicit gaps; a missing measurement is not zero.

steps.title: Specify a segment cost
steps.text: Choose a count likelihood, such as an exposure-adjusted Poisson or negative binomial, and calculate negative log likelihood within each candidate segment.

steps.title: Optimize boundaries
steps.text: PELT minimizes the sum of segment costs plus a penalty per changepoint; it is an optimization algorithm, not a particular likelihood.

steps.title: Quantify uncertainty
steps.text: Vary penalty and assumptions, and assess boundary stability with a suitable resampling or independent dataset.

steps.title: Add conditional alleles
steps.text: Only after auditing shared molecules and phase, test an explicitly derived conditional allele model; otherwise report depth and allele evidence separately.

example.title: A boundary on a count grid
example.setup: Four equally exposed bins contain 10, 12, 4, 3 counts.
steps: A one-segment Poisson model uses mean 7.25.
A two-segment model after bin 2 uses means 11 and 3.5 and fits the counts better.
Keep the split only if the likelihood improvement exceeds the chosen changepoint penalty.
example.interpretation: A retained boundary is a relative count change; accessibility or technical bias can also cause it.

needed: Independent validation and conditional measurement model
adaptation.first_experiment: Freeze a grid and compare depth-only boundaries across penalties and held-out cells.
adaptation.success: Stable boundaries and calibrated uncertainty across independent datasets, with explicit abstention where coverage is weak.

cautions: This is a proposed diagnostic, not existing pyEpiAneufinder statistical behavior.
Selecting boundaries and testing them on the same data can bias significance.
A categorical loss or depth zero does not establish absolute zero copies.

name: Covariance-aware joint segmentation / Bayesian HMM
tagline: Proposed joint model that explicitly represents dependence and missing evidence.

steps.title: Describe observations
steps.text: Define depth and SNP-site allele counts, exposure, phase blocks and whether measurements share fragments.

steps.title: Write a joint emission
steps.text: Use a justified shared-fragment generative model or an empirically supported covariance model; do not simply multiply dependent likelihoods.

steps.title: Handle partial observations
steps.text: Marginalize an unavailable component under an explicit missingness assumption; an observed count of zero remains an observation.

steps.title: Model state continuity
steps.text: Assign genomic-distance-aware transition probabilities between candidate states and allow phase-block orientation uncertainty.

steps.title: Infer and check
steps.text: Combine emissions and transitions to obtain boundary or state uncertainty, then check calibration and abstain where the model is uninformative.

example.title: One missing allele bin
example.setup: Three bins have relative depth 1.0, 0.5, 0.5; the last has no callable allele observations.
steps: Use depth evidence in all three bins and allele evidence only where measured.
A state transition after bin 1 competes with the prior favoring continuity.
The last bin contributes no invented balanced allele count; the transition and neighboring data still influence its posterior.
example.interpretation: Missingness can itself be informative, so marginalization is valid only under justified assumptions.

needed: SNP phase blocks and molecule-level counting
adaptation.first_experiment: Measure shared fragments and phase orientation before constructing simulated joint data.
adaptation.success: Held-out boundary coverage and false positives remain calibrated under sparse and correlated observations.

cautions: The model is proposed and unvalidated; its covariance can be difficult to estimate at low coverage.
A posterior reflects the chosen priors and likelihood, not independent biological validation.
AT site counts can duplicate molecules; phase orientation is not established.

name: FACETS joint CBS and ASCAT / ASPCF
tagline: Related bulk DNA approaches combine depth and allele information but solve different problems.

steps.title: Measure paired signals
steps.text: FACETS uses tumor and matched-normal sequencing at SNPs to construct total-depth and allele-imbalance signals; matched normal helps correct allele-specific biases.

steps.title: Segment jointly
steps.text: FACETS uses multivariate rank-based circular binary segmentation (CBS) to locate shared changes in total-depth and allele-imbalance signals; sparse heterozygous sites carry limited allele information.

steps.title: Infer states
steps.text: FACETS uses segmented signals and a purity/ploidy model to estimate allele-specific copy number under candidate solutions.

steps.title: Use ASCAT separately
steps.text: ASCAT is a separate algorithm: it uses allele-specific tumor and normal signals, allele-specific piecewise constant fitting (ASPCF), and models tumor admixture and ploidy to infer allele-specific states. ASPCF is not FACETS CBS.

steps.title: Compare candidate solutions
steps.text: Inspect ambiguity and compare independent evidence; neither method is automatically transferable from bulk DNA to sparse ATAC.

example.title: Same depth, different allele balance
example.setup: Two hypothetical regions have equal normalized total depth; one has balanced alleles and the other has a persistent imbalance.
steps: Joint segmentation can consider an allele shift even without a depth shift.
A purity/ploidy solution proposes allele-specific states compatible with both signals.
Another purity or baseline may also fit; assess alternative solutions.
example.interpretation: Imbalance is informative but does not uniquely determine absolute copy number without identifiable assumptions.

needed: Matched normal or other defensible bias controls
adaptation.first_experiment: Use these methods as conceptual comparators on external paired-DNA benchmark data before considering adaptation.
adaptation.success: Reproduce benchmark behavior and make solution ambiguity visible.

cautions: Published DNA and array methods are not drop-in scATAC callers.
No matched normal or diploid anchor is assumed locally.
Depth and alleles can share fragments, and accessibility can confound dosage.

name: Blind-spot image denoising / Noise2Self
tagline: Predict masked observations for denoising; predictions are not new evidence.

steps.title: Choose masking groups
steps.text: Partition features into groups and hide each target group from the predictor used for it.

steps.title: Predict from other features
steps.text: Train or tune a predictor using surrounding or related observations while preventing direct access to the masked value.

steps.title: Use self-supervised loss
steps.text: Compare the masked prediction with the noisy held-out measurement; under appropriate independent-noise assumptions this can assess denoising risk.

steps.title: Check assumptions
steps.text: Test whether noise dependence, spatial correlation and sparse coverage invalidate the masking design.

steps.title: Keep predictions separate
steps.text: Display any prediction as an exploratory imputation and retain the original observed data and missingness mask.

example.title: A masked middle bin
steps: Hide the middle value from the predictor.
A simple neighbor-based predictor might return 9.
Compare that prediction with the held-out measured zero when evaluating prediction error.
example.interpretation: The predicted 9 is not an observed count; a genuine boundary or correlated noise can make smoothing misleading.

adaptation.first_experiment: Test denoising only on controlled synthetic data with known boundaries and realistic correlations.
adaptation.success: Predictions preserve boundaries and uncertainty in independent tests; raw evidence remains available.

cautions: Noise2Self was not established as a CN segmentation method for this assay.
Imputation can blur boundaries or invent apparent allele evidence.
Do not fill missing alleles and then treat predictions as measurements.

name: Poisson / negative binomial exposure regression
tagline: Proposed relative count modeling starts by asking how many zeros sampling predicts.

steps.title: Define counts and exposure
steps.text: Use raw regional counts, callable span, per-cell exposure and carefully selected covariates.

steps.title: Fit a mean model
steps.text: Relate log expected count to log exposure plus region and covariate effects; interpret coefficients as relative rates.

steps.title: Compare distributions
steps.text: A Poisson model has variance μ; NB2 permits variance μ + μ²/r, accommodating extra variability for finite r.

steps.title: Predict zeros
steps.text: Poisson predicts P(0)=exp(−μ); NB2 predicts P(0)=(r/(r+μ))^r. Compare predictions with held-out observations.

steps.title: Report uncertainty
steps.text: Assess rate contrasts and model fit without treating the reference or a cluster as automatically diploid.

example.title: A low mean produces zeros
example.setup: For illustration take μ=0.5 counts per cell and NB2 dispersion parameter r=1.
steps: Poisson predicts exp(−0.5) ≈ 0.607 zeros.
NB2 predicts (1/1.5)^1 ≈ 0.667 zeros.
Compare these baseline predictions with held-out zeros rather than treating every zero as a deletion.
example.interpretation: These numbers are illustrations, not fitted parameters or evidence of a biological state.

adaptation.first_experiment: Fit Poisson and NB models on training cells and compare held-out zero rates by exposure.
adaptation.success: Predictive calibration and stable relative effects across datasets.

cautions: Accessibility, mappability and dosage are confounded.
Cluster adjustment may remove signal if cluster membership is coverage-confounded.
Selecting and testing the same region on the same data can bias inference.

name: Phase-aware beta-binomial allele model
tagline: Proposed regional allele evidence accounts for overdispersion and unknown phase.

steps.title: Audit allele counts
steps.text: Join cells by barcode and retain HA, HB and AT with callable masks; AT=0 supplies no allele fraction.

steps.title: Establish orientation
steps.text: Determine SNP phase sets and orientation; model switches or avoid pooling blocks whose orientation is unknown.

steps.title: Condition on total
steps.text: For A count k out of n, a binomial model assumes independent trials with fixed fraction p; a beta-binomial allows p to vary according to a beta distribution.

steps.title: Estimate uncertainty
steps.text: Use an appropriate prior or fit dispersion from sufficient data, accounting for bias and ascertainment; sparse observations give broad intervals.

steps.title: Interpret alongside depth
steps.text: Report allele imbalance and its uncertainty separately from dosage unless a justified joint measurement model is available.

example.title: Four allele observations
example.setup: In one oriented block, HA=3 and HB=1, so AT=4 and the observed HA fraction is 0.75.
steps: Under a binomial model with p=0.5, exactly three HA counts occur with probability 4/16 = 0.25.
A beta-binomial permits extra variation and can make extreme counts more plausible than a fixed-p binomial.
With AT=0 the fraction is undefined, not 0.5.
example.interpretation: Four observations give weak evidence; this example is not a fitted or calibrated test.

needed: Bias controls, SNP ascertainment and count-unit audit
adaptation.first_experiment: Measure phase continuity and simulate power across plausible coverage and dispersion.
adaptation.success: Intervals and false-positive rates are calibrated, with explicit insufficient-evidence outcomes.

cautions: One molecule may contribute to multiple SNP sites; counts are not automatically independent trials.
Opposing haplotype orientations or mixed states can cancel imbalance.
Allele fraction alone cannot identify a 0:0 state.

name: Hurdle, zero-inflated NB or latent count mixtures
tagline: Proposed alternatives separate zero mechanisms only when diagnostics justify the complexity.

steps.title: Fit baseline models
steps.text: Start with exposure-adjusted Poisson and negative binomial predictive checks, including zeros by exposure.

steps.title: Define a ZINB model
steps.text: A zero-inflated negative binomial mixes a point mass at zero with an NB distribution; either component can produce an observed zero.

steps.title: Define a hurdle model
steps.text: A hurdle model separately models zero versus positive occurrence, then models positive counts with a zero-truncated distribution.

steps.title: Compare held-out predictions
steps.text: Assess calibration, stability and predictive performance across cells and independent datasets; low means and heterogeneity can already produce many zeros.

steps.title: Calibrate comparisons
steps.text: Mixture parameters can be unidentified or on a boundary, so ordinary chi-square likelihood-ratio approximations may fail; use a justified calibrated procedure.

example.title: Two ways to generate zero
example.setup: Suppose a ZINB model assigns point-mass probability 0.2 and its NB component predicts zero probability 0.5.
steps: The total zero probability is 0.2 + 0.8 × 0.5 = 0.6.
In a hurdle model with zero probability 0.6, the positive-count component is conditional on being positive.
Both predict 60% zeros but tell different stories about positive counts.
example.interpretation: Equal zero rates do not establish the same mechanism; these values are illustrative, not fitted.

needed: Mixture identifiability and calibrated model comparison
adaptation.first_experiment: Compare baseline NB and alternative predictive distributions on held-out data before interpreting components.
adaptation.success: Improved reproducible calibration without unstable parameters; biological labels require independent evidence.

cautions: A statistical zero component is not proof of biallelic deletion.
Small means and unmodeled heterogeneity can mimic excess zeros.
Component interpretation and significance are sensitive to model assumptions.
